title: Battle of Plassey
description: The East India Company defeated Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah at Plassey. The battle became a decisive turning point in Bengal's political history and enabled the Company to establish growing control over the region.

title: Battle of Buxar
description: The East India Company defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Mughal emperor Shah Alam II. The victory consolidated Company military power in Bengal and northern India.

title: East India Company receives Diwani rights
description: Mughal emperor Shah Alam II granted the East India Company the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. This gave the Company authority over revenue collection in much of eastern India.

title: Great Bengal Famine
description: A catastrophic famine struck Bengal after crop failures and severe economic and administrative pressures. Contemporary and later estimates indicate an enormous loss of life across the affected region.

title: Calcutta becomes the centre of Company administration
description: Calcutta became the principal centre of East India Company administration in Bengal. Its political, commercial and intellectual importance grew rapidly during the following century.

title: Permanent Settlement of Bengal
description: The Permanent Settlement established a new land-revenue system in Bengal and recognised zamindars as hereditary landholders subject to fixed revenue obligations. It profoundly influenced Bengal's rural social and economic structure.

title: Fort William College established
description: Fort William College was established in Calcutta to train Company officials in Indian languages. Its activities contributed to the development and standardisation of modern prose in several Indian languages, including Bengali.

title: Hindu College established
description: Hindu College was established in Calcutta with the support of Indian reformers and European educators. It became an important centre for Western-style education and intellectual change in 19th-century Bengal.

title: Birth of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
description: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was born in Birsingha. He later became an influential educator, Sanskrit scholar, social reformer and important contributor to the development of modern Bengali prose.

title: Birth of Michael Madhusudan Dutt
description: Michael Madhusudan Dutt was born in Sagardari. He became a major figure in modern Bengali poetry and introduced new forms, themes and influences into Bengali literature.

title: Brahmo Samaj established
description: Raja Ram Mohan Roy established the Brahmo Sabha in Calcutta, later known as the Brahmo Samaj. It became an important centre of religious and social reform in Bengal.

title: Abolition of Sati in British India
description: The Bengal Sati Regulation prohibited the practice of sati in territories under the Bengal Presidency. Raja Ram Mohan Roy had campaigned strongly against the practice.

title: Birth of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay
description: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay was born in Naihati. He became one of the central figures in the development of the modern Bengali novel and Bengali prose.

title: Vidyasagar's work on Bengali education and prose
description: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar's educational work and Bengali textbooks helped establish clearer prose, spelling and pedagogical conventions. His later Barnaparichay became one of the best-known Bengali primers.

title: Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act
description: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act legalised widow remarriage among Hindus under British Indian law. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a leading advocate for the reform.

title: Indian Rebellion of 1857 in Bengal
description: The rebellion against Company rule reached several parts of Bengal and eastern India. Its failure led to the end of East India Company rule and the establishment of direct British Crown rule.

title: Beginning of direct British Crown rule
description: Following the rebellion of 1857, the British Crown assumed direct control over India. Bengal remained one of the most important administrative, economic and intellectual regions of British India.

title: Birth of Rabindranath Tagore
description: Rabindranath Tagore was born in Calcutta. He became one of the most influential figures in Bengali literature, music and culture and later received the Nobel Prize in Literature.

title: Birth of Swami Vivekananda
description: Swami Vivekananda was born in Calcutta. He became an important religious and cultural figure and played a significant role in presenting Indian philosophical traditions internationally.

title: Birth of Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay
description: Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay was born in Debanandapur. He later became one of the most widely read Bengali novelists, writing extensively about society, relationships and ordinary lives.

title: Indian National Congress founded
description: The Indian National Congress was founded in Bombay, beginning a major phase of organised Indian nationalism. Bengal subsequently became one of the principal centres of the nationalist movement.

title: Vivekananda speaks at the Parliament of Religions
description: Swami Vivekananda addressed the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago. His appearance brought a Bengali-born Indian religious thinker to international attention.

title: Ramakrishna Mission founded
description: Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in Calcutta. The organisation combined spiritual activities with education, healthcare and social service.

title: Tagore establishes his school at Santiniketan
description: Rabindranath Tagore established a school at Santiniketan based on an educational philosophy centred on nature, creativity and learning beyond conventional classroom structures.

title: First Partition of Bengal
description: The British government divided Bengal and created the province of Eastern Bengal and Assam. The decision triggered widespread opposition, including the Swadeshi and boycott movements.

title: Swadeshi Movement in Bengal
description: The partition of Bengal stimulated the Swadeshi movement, which promoted boycotts of imported goods and encouraged indigenous industry and education. Bengal became a major centre of anti-colonial political mobilisation.

title: All-India Muslim League founded in Dhaka
description: The All-India Muslim League was founded during a meeting in Dhaka. It later became a major political force in the movement that resulted in the creation of Pakistan.

title: Partition of Bengal annulled
description: The British government annulled the 1905 partition of Bengal. At the same time, the capital of British India was moved from Calcutta to Delhi.

title: Rabindranath Tagore receives Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Rabindranath Tagore received the Nobel Prize in Literature. He became the first Asian Nobel laureate and Bengali literature gained unprecedented international recognition.

title: Kazi Nazrul Islam emerges in Bengali literary life
description: Kazi Nazrul Islam's early literary and journalistic work began gaining attention around this period. He would become one of the most influential Bengali poets of the 20th century.

title: University of Dhaka established
description: The University of Dhaka was established in British Bengal. It became an important centre of education and later played a major role in the cultural and political history of East Bengal.

title: Nazrul's Bidrohi and the rise of the Rebel Poet
description: Kazi Nazrul Islam's poem Bidrohi became a landmark of modern Bengali poetry. His writing introduced powerful themes of rebellion, equality and resistance.

title: Chittagong Armoury Raid
description: Surya Sen and revolutionary associates attacked British armouries in Chittagong. The raid became one of the best-known episodes of Bengal's revolutionary anti-colonial movement.

title: Publication of Pather Panchali
description: Bibhutibhushan Bandyopadhyay's Pather Panchali was published as a novel. Its depiction of rural Bengal became a landmark of modern Bengali literature.

title: Bengal Famine
description: A devastating famine struck Bengal during the Second World War. Food availability, wartime policies, inflation, distribution problems and other factors contributed to a severe humanitarian disaster.

title: Great Calcutta Killings
description: Communal violence erupted in Calcutta following Direct Action Day. Thousands were killed or injured, deepening political and communal tensions in Bengal shortly before Partition.

title: Partition of Bengal
description: The end of British rule divided Bengal into West Bengal, which joined India, and East Bengal, which joined Pakistan. The partition caused large-scale migration and permanently changed Bengal's political geography.

title: Radcliffe boundary announced
description: The boundary between India and Pakistan in Bengal was formally announced through the Radcliffe Award. The new border divided communities, districts, transport networks and economic regions.

title: Bengali Language Movement begins
description: After the creation of Pakistan, demands grew in East Bengal for Bengali to receive recognition as a state language. Students and intellectuals became central to the movement.

title: Bengali Language Movement of 1952
description: Students and activists in Dhaka protested for recognition of Bengali as a state language of Pakistan. Police opened fire on demonstrators, making 21 February a defining date in Bengali linguistic history.

title: United Front wins East Bengal election
description: The United Front won a decisive victory in the East Bengal legislative election. The result demonstrated strong support for regional political demands within East Pakistan.

title: Bengali recognised as a state language of Pakistan
description: Pakistan's constitution recognised Bengali alongside Urdu as a state language. The recognition followed years of political and cultural mobilisation around Bengali language rights.

title: Bengali Language Movement in Silchar
description: Bengali-speaking protesters in Silchar demonstrated over the official use of Bengali. Eleven people were killed in police firing, and Bengali subsequently received official recognition in the Barak Valley.

title: Six-Point Movement
description: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman presented the Six-Point Programme demanding extensive autonomy for East Pakistan. It became a major milestone in the development of Bengali political nationalism.

title: Mass Uprising of 1969
description: A mass uprising spread across East Pakistan against the Ayub Khan regime. The movement strengthened Bengali political mobilisation and contributed to the collapse of Ayub Khan's rule.

title: Pakistan general election
description: The Awami League won a majority of seats in Pakistan's National Assembly, largely through its overwhelming support in East Pakistan. The transfer of power did not occur, leading to a major political crisis.

title: 7 March Speech
description: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman delivered a landmark speech at the Ramna Race Course in Dhaka during the political crisis in East Pakistan. The speech became a defining moment in the history of Bengali nationalism.

title: Operation Searchlight
description: The Pakistan Army launched a military operation in East Pakistan on 25 March. The crackdown marked the beginning of widespread violence and the armed conflict that became the Bangladesh Liberation War.

title: Declaration of Bangladesh's Independence
description: Bangladesh's independence was proclaimed in the context of the military crackdown and political crisis in East Pakistan. The declaration marked the beginning of the country's formal struggle for independence.

title: Bangladesh Liberation War
description: A nine-month war followed the political and military crisis in East Pakistan. The conflict involved Bengali resistance forces, Pakistani forces and Indian military intervention, ending with the creation of Bangladesh.

title: Victory and creation of Bangladesh
description: Pakistani forces in East Pakistan surrendered on 16 December. Bangladesh emerged as an independent sovereign state with Bengali language and culture at the centre of its national identity.

title: Constitution of Bangladesh adopted
description: Bangladesh's Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly. Bengali was established as the state language, reflecting the central role of language in the country's political identity.

title: Bangladesh joins the United Nations
description: Bangladesh was admitted to the United Nations as a member state. Its admission marked an important step in the international recognition of the new Bengali-majority country.

title: Assassination of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
description: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the founding leader of Bangladesh, was assassinated in a military coup. The event marked a major political rupture in the country's early history.

title: Death of Kazi Nazrul Islam
description: Kazi Nazrul Islam died in Dhaka after spending the final years of his life in Bangladesh. He remains one of the most influential figures in Bengali poetry, music and cultural history.

title: Bangla Language Implementation Act
description: Bangladesh enacted legislation requiring Bangla to be used in government offices, courts and other official functions. The law strengthened the institutional position of Bengali in the country.

title: Mass Uprising against Ershad
description: A broad-based mass movement led to the resignation of President H. M. Ershad. The uprising became a major turning point in Bangladesh's transition toward parliamentary democracy.

title: Parliamentary democracy restored in Bangladesh
description: Following the 1990 mass uprising, parliamentary government was restored through constitutional change and national elections. Bangladesh entered a new phase of competitive parliamentary politics.

title: International Mother Language Day proclaimed
description: UNESCO proclaimed 21 February as International Mother Language Day. The date commemorates the Bengali Language Movement and has become an international observance promoting linguistic and cultural diversity.

title: Political transition in West Bengal and TMC era starts
description: The 2011 West Bengal Assembly election ended more than three decades of uninterrupted Left Front government in the state. The change marked a major political transition in contemporary West Bengal.
